notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11 and later. Uses form POST for this documented mutation. Changes can affect package or account capabilities; this method performs one request with no retry or rollback.
Package names cannot be renamed, and addPackage forbids the name extensions. Creation does not implicitly assign an account to the package.

Omitted options retain upstream defaults, including default feature list, server theme/locale and resource limits. Omitted packageExtensions means no extensions; upstream recommends the separate extension helpers. Names/variables are case-sensitive; arbitrary extension variables are not represented by this fixed-parameter method. A server without the Web Server role defaults CGI off and cannot enable it. FrontPage settings are ignored.

Bandwidth, disk quota and mailbox quota use MB. Zero, unlimited and documented null mean unlimited for bandwidth/disk/mailbox quota, subject to unlimited ACL permissions; email rate limits also use zero or unlimited. Count limits document unlimited or null separately from zero. The scalar encoder omits explicit PHP null, so it does not send a JSON null sentinel; use documented zero/unlimited when required. SQL limits apply separately to each available SQL engine. Omitted optional arguments are not filled with defaults.

Keep exact wire-name differences: addPackage uses uppercase MAX_DEFER_FAIL_PERCENTAGE and MAX_EMAIL_PER_HOUR, while editPackage uses lowercase names; max_emailacct_quota and max_team_users are lowercase on both. Digest authentication and CGI/shell switches are boolean inputs encoded as 0/1; IP uses y/n. The pinned max_team_users input is an integer; its source does not declare explicit null.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11 and later. Uses form POST for this documented mutation. Changes can affect package or account capabilities; this method performs one request with no retry or rollback.
Package names cannot be renamed, and addPackage forbids the name extensions. editPackage creates a missing package and applies changes to every account already on the package.

Omitting featurelist assigns the default feature list to the plan's accounts, and omitting packageExtensions means the plan has no extensions. Omission can reset existing settings across every account using the plan; it is not a preserve-current-value operation. Upstream recommends the separate extension helpers. Extension names and variables are case-sensitive. A server without the Web Server role defaults CGI off and cannot enable it. FrontPage settings are ignored.

Bandwidth, disk quota and mailbox quota use MB. Zero, unlimited and documented null mean unlimited for bandwidth/disk/mailbox quota, subject to unlimited ACL permissions; email rate limits also use zero or unlimited. Count limits document unlimited or null separately from zero. SQL limits apply separately to each available SQL engine.

Keep exact wire-name differences: addPackage uses uppercase MAX_DEFER_FAIL_PERCENTAGE and MAX_EMAIL_PER_HOUR, while editPackage uses lowercase names; max_emailacct_quota and max_team_users are lowercase on both. Digest authentication and CGI/shell switches are boolean inputs encoded as 0/1; IP uses y/n. Changing maxEmailacctQuota does not affect existing email accounts.

Client behavior: read the current plan with getPackageInfo() before editing, then explicitly send the complete intended settings, including featurelist and packageExtensions, to avoid unintended resets. The client does not read, merge or fill settings automatically. PHP null omits an argument rather than sending a null sentinel or preserving its server value. Arbitrary extension variables are outside this fixed-parameter method.
